# Adjudication Task — Chapter 1056

## Korean source

```text
  1|＃1056화
  2|
  3|
  4|
  5|슈확!
  6|
  7|바람을 찢은 섬광은 실로 예리하면서도 정확했다.
  8|
  9|흑룡도(黑龍刀).
 10|
 11|고작 십 대에 불과했던, 그러나 어린 나이를 무색하게 만들 만큼 일찍이 두각을 드러냈던 한 소년이 아버지에게 처음이자 마지막으로 선물 받았던 보도(寶刀)는, 주인의 손을 따라 눈앞의 목표를 정확히 베어 갈랐다.
 12|
 13|서걱!
 14|
 15|서늘한 절삭음과 함께 핏물이 튀었고, 이 모든 것을 직시하고 있던 한 쌍의 눈동자가 깊게 가라앉았다.
 16|
 17|“무슨 짓이냐.”
 18|
 19|많은 것이 담긴 물음이었지만, 되돌아온 대답은 간단명료했다.
 20|
 21|“제가 원하는 길이 아니기 때문입니다.”
 22|
 23|사마표는 차갑게 식은 칼자루에서 손을 뗐다.
 24|
 25|흑룡마문의 후계자에게만 허락된 그 예리한 날붙이는, 사마공의 콧날을 스쳐 지나가 피 웅덩이를 가른 후였다.
 26|
 27|진정한 사파인으로 성장한 아들의 모습에 기뻐하며, 기꺼이 죽음을 받아들였던 아버지를 비웃듯이.
 28|
 29|“이게 제 선택입니다. 당신의 뒤를 이어 흑룡마문의 문주가 될, 이 사마표가 택한 길입니다.”
 30|
 31|“어째서……!”
 32|
 33|핏물이 끓어오르는 목소리로 외치는 사마공을, 사마표는 담담한 눈빛으로 응시했다.
 34|
 35|“옳지 않기 때문입니다.”
 36|
 37|“뭐라?”
 38|
 39|“최선(最先)이나, 최선(最善)이 아니기 때문입니다.”
 40|
 41|사마표에게 있어, 이것은 무엇이 먼저냐의 문제가 아니었다.
 42|
 43|무엇이 옳은가, 더욱 선한가의 문제였다.
 44|
 45|“일평생 잊고 있었습니다. 아니, 익숙해져 있었기에 계속해서 모른 척해 왔습니다. 하지만 이제는 아닙니다.”
 46|
 47|감숙에서의 지난 삶은, 그야말로 투쟁의 연속이었다.
 48|
 49|앞서 태어난 피붙이들이 그러했듯, 사마가(家)의 막내 역시 버림받지 않기 위해 발버둥 쳐야 했다.
 50|
 51|그들은 같은 핏줄을 지닌 가족인 동시에, 오직 하나뿐인 후계자 자리를 다퉈야 하는 경쟁자였으며, 이러한 핏줄을 물려준 한 사람에게 복종하는 군인이나 다름없었다.
 52|
 53|때로는 죽음조차 불사해야 하는, 그런 존재.
 54|
 55|
 56|
 57|‘아버지, 둘째 형님께서……!’
 58|
 59|‘이미 전령을 통해 들었다. 장례는 놈들을 모조리 쓸어 버린 후에 치를 것이니, 그리 알고 있거라.’
 60|
 61|
 62|
 63|사마공은 냉철한 정복자였고, 사파를 일통하기 위해서는 그만한 피와 희생이 필요했다.
 64|
 65|흑룡마문이 천하의 모든 사파를 아우르고 공동파와 어깨를 나란히 하는 과정에서, 다섯이 넘는 형제와 누이가 죽음을 맞이했다는 사실은 공공연한 비밀이었다.
 66|
 67|불과 십 대의 나이임에도 후계자로 낙점된 흑룡마문의 막내 공자가, 보이는 것만큼 냉정하지 않다는 사실은 누구도 몰랐지만.
 68|
 69|
 70|
 71|‘어찌 그리 서럽게 울고 있느냐?’
 72|
 73|‘아버지, 흑룡마문 도왔다. 그런데 죽었다. 슬프다.’
 74|
 75|‘……!’
 76|
 77|‘시신, 찾아야 한다. 아버지 묻어 줘야 한다. 그런데, 그런데 저 사람들이 모른다고 했다. 태산이 슬프다.’
 78|
 79|‘……태산이라고 했지, 따라오거라.’
 80|
 81|
 82|
 83|사마표는 산만 한 덩치로 울고 있는 소년의 아버지를 찾아 주었다. 흑룡마문의 무복을 입은 채, 까마귀 떼에 둘러싸여 있던 그를 정성 들여 묻었다.
 84|
 85|그리고 생전 처음으로 친구를 얻었다.
 86|
 87|가족보다 소중한, 아버지보다 자신을 아껴 주는 유일한 친구를.
 88|
 89|하지만 그로부터 십여 년의 세월이 흐른 후, 또 다른 친구들이 생길 것이라고는 생각하지 못했다.
 90|
 91|“그들과 함께 지내며 알게 되었습니다. 모든 것은 결국 제 선택에 따라 달라진다는 것을.”
 92|
 93|화룡각.
 94|
 95|그 거창한 이름과는 달리, 고작 열 명도 되지 않는 그들의 틈바구니에서 사마표는 자신이 몰랐던 새로운 길을 발견할 수 있었다.
 96|
 97|그곳에서는 어떤 족쇄나 꼬리표도 존재하지 않았다.
 98|
 99|언제나 서로를 믿고 싸웠고, 그렇게 위기를 헤쳐 나갔다.
100|
101|아마도 그래서였을 것이다.
102|
103|사마표가 자신의 지난 삶을 몇 번이나 되돌아보게 된 이유도.
104|
105|어느 순간부터, 피도 눈물도 없는 아버지에 대해 낯선 감정이 들기 시작한 이유도.
106|
107|“문득 그런 생각이 들었습니다. 알고 보면 당신도, 퍽 불쌍한 사람이라는 생각이.”
108|
109|“……!”
110|
111|“처음부터 그러지는 않았겠지요. 서서히 야망에 사로잡히고, 어느 날부터인가 수단과 방법을 가리지 않게 되었겠지요.”
112|
113|한때, 아버지의 냉엄한 시선을 차마 마주칠 수 없었던 아들은 이제 없다.
114|
115|지금 이 순간, 사마표는 담담하면서도 슬픔이 담긴 눈빛으로 죽음을 코앞에 둔 아버지를 바라보고 있었다.
116|
117|“우연이 아니었습니다.”
118|
119|“그게…… 무슨.”
120|
121|“우연히 돌아온 것이 아닙니다. 그저, 당신의 마지막을 지키기 위해 온 겁니다. 흑야왕의 후계자가 아니라, 사마공의 피를 이어받은 아들로서.”
122|
123|철벅.
124|
125|“알고 계십니까?”
126|
127|사마표는 피 웅덩이에 앉아 자신의 아버지와 시선을 맞추었다. 떨리는 그의 눈동자를 바라보며 천천히 말을 이었다.
128|
129|“아버지를 죽일 수 있는 아들은, 이 세상에 없습니다.”
130|
131|“……!”
132|
133|“제 입으로 직접 저들에게 모든 사실을 밝힐 겁니다. 아버지의 배신을 애써 모른 척해 왔던 못난 아들에 관한 이야기도 털어놓겠습니다.”
134|
135|“너.”
136|
137|“용서받고자 하는 것이 아닙니다. 감내하려는 것입니다.”
138|
139|모든 것을 받아들인 평온한 그 대답에, 사마공은 아무 말도 할 수 없었다.
140|
141|그저 오랫동안 잊고 있던, 오늘 이 자리에서야 문득 떠올린 어떤 감정을 억누르기 위해 안간힘을 쓸 뿐이었다.
142|
143|서서히 어두워지는 시야 속. 마지막을 암시하듯 가빠지는 숨결을 느끼며.
144|
145|“왜 그랬냐고, 물었었지. 일평생 생존과 실리만을 좇던 내가 왜 그런 멍청한 선택을 했느냐고…….”
146|
147|자신의 모든 것을 물려줄 후계자를 구하기 위해서?
148|
149|아니다. 아니었다.
150|
151|적어도 그때 그 순간만큼은, 또 다른 이유였음을 사마공은 알고 있었다.
152|
153|다만, 이를 고백하기에는 너무 늦었을 뿐.
154|
155|“나는, 이 아비는.”
156|
157|아버지의 최후를 지키기 위해 돌아온 아들을 향해, 사마공은 남아 있는 온 힘을 다해 목소리를 쥐어 짜냈다.
158|
159|그것이 자신의 마지막 숨결이라는 사실조차 인식하지 못한 채.
160|
161|스륵.
162|
163|불현듯 꺾이는 고개.
164|
165|살아생전의 업보처럼, 처참한 모습으로 죽음을 맞이한 아버지를 향해 아들은 나직이 속삭였다.
166|
167|“들었습니다. 분명히.”
168|
169|이내 들썩이는 어깨를 따라, 두 부자(父子)를 적신 피웅덩이가 잘게 떨리고 있었다.
170|
171|
172|
173|* * *
174|
175|
176|
177|극도로 훈련된 사냥개들은 언제나 주인의 명령을 따라 움직인다.
178|
179|주인이 가리킨 사냥감을 직시하고, 이빨을 드러내며 으르렁대다가, 마침내 목줄이 풀림과 동시에 온 힘을 다해 달려나가 물어뜯는 것이다.
180|
181|사냥감의 숨통이 끊어질 때까지.
182|
183|혹은 사냥을 그만하고 되돌아오라는 주인의 명령이 떨어지기 전까지.
184|
185|바로 지금처럼.
186|
187|쐐애액!
188|
189|측면으로부터 시작된, 강렬한 파공성과 함께 번뜩이는 섬광.
190|
191|그러나 속도란 늘 상대적인 것이다.
192|
193|새하얀 검신을 타고 솟구친 검기(劍氣)가 정수리를 향해 떨어져 내리는 그 일련의 과정은 절정 고수의 솜씨답게 쾌속했지만, 내게는 아니었다.
194|
195|서걱!
196|
197|일순간 갈라지는 공간.
198|
199|반 박자 늦은 절삭음과 함께, 은백색의 창날이 스쳐 지나간 궤적 안의 모든 것이 베어졌다.
200|
201|어느새 바람 앞의 촛불처럼 꺼져버린 검기.
202|
203|그 강력한 기운을 담고 있던 검신.
204|
205|마지막으로 이 덧없는 공격을 감행한 누군가의 몸뚱어리까지.
206|
207|푸확!
208|
209|군더더기 없이 깔끔하게 분리된 몸뚱어리에서 엄청난 양의 피 분수가 뿜어져 나왔지만, 그 처참한 광경에도 나는 눈 하나 깜짝하지 않았다.
210|
211|지금 이 순간에도 사방에서 달려드는, 또 다른 사냥개들 역시 마찬가지였다.
212|
213|푹, 콰득! 퍼걱!
214|
215|가장 먼저 전방에서 달려드는 놈의 가슴에 창날을 박아넣고, 곧이어 사각에서 들이닥친 적의 얼굴을 일권(一拳)으로 짓뭉개는 동시에 박혀있던 창날을 뽑아 휘둘렀다.
216|
217|“꺼흑, 끅.”
218|
219|털썩.
220|
221|유언을 대신한 단말마(斷末摩)와 동시에 쓰러지는 세 명의 절정 고수.
222|
223|아니, 세 구의 시체.
224|
225|하지만 피로 물든 설원을 휘감은 전투의 광기는, 조금도 사그라질 기미가 보이지 않았다.
226|
227|쉬쉬쉬쉭!
228|
229|찰나의 공백조차 허락하지 않고 빈 자리를 메우며 달려드는 암천의 교도들.
230|
231|그리고 한 줌의 감정조차 깃들어있지 않은 그 무감각한 표정과 눈동자들을 보며, 나는 전신을 짓누르는 극심한 피로를 느꼈다.
232|
233|‘도대체 몇 명째지?’
234|
235|모르겠다.
236|
237|내 손에 죽음을 맞이한 적들의 숫자를 일일이 헤아릴 여유도, 그럴 이유도 없었으니까.
238|
239|그저 싸울 뿐이다. 끊임없이 쓰러트릴 뿐이다.
240|
241|영혼이 없는 저 목각 인형들을.
242|
243|자신들의 목줄을 쥔 주인이 사라졌음에도 불구하고, 마지막으로 내려진 명령을 따라 맹목적으로 임무를 수행하고 있는 저 사냥개이자 부나방들을.
244|
245|물론 나 역시 알고 있다.
246|
247|이건 일방적인 학살이고, 살육이다.
248|
249|그러나 반드시 해내야 했다.
250|
251|그것만이 피로 얼룩진 이 혈투를 끝내는 유일한 방법이자, 한 사람이라도 더 많은 아군을 구할 수 있는 길이니까.
252|
253|그렇기에 나는 당장이라도 끊어질 것 같은 이 의식의 끈을, 온 힘을 다해 붙잡을 수밖에 없었다.
254|
255|‘와라.’
256|
257|나는 마음속으로 뇌까리며 적들을 향해 쇄도했다.
258|
259|정확히는, 쇄도하려 했다.
260|
261|바로 그 순간, 아득해지는 시야를 느끼기 전까지는.
262|
263|“……!”
264|
265|머릿속에서 붉은색 경종이 울렸다.
266|
267|한참 전부터 한계에 달해있던 정신력이 참지 못하고 전달한 위험신호.
268|
269|하지만 내가 애써 이를 악물며 눈을 부릅떴을 때는, 이미 모든 것이 늦어 있었다.
270|
271|슈확!
272|
273|어느샌가 비스듬히 기울어진 시야 속, 나도 모르는 사이에 휘청이고 만 몸뚱어리를 향해 십여 자루의 날붙이가 쏟아지고 있었다.
274|
275|흐릿하면서도, 느리게.
276|
277|문제는 극도로 예리한 안력(眼力)과는 달리, 빠르게 명령을 내려 몸을 움직여야 할 두뇌가 석상처럼 굳어있다는 것이었다.
278|
279|‘빌어먹을.’
280|
281|느려진 세상 속, 나는 내심 욕설을 내뱉었다.
282|
283|저들은 혈검마군도, 대술사도, 흑귀들과 비견될 만한 무위를 지니지도 않았다.
284|
285|아니, 턱없이 부족하다.
286|
287|평상시의 나였다면 코웃음을 쳤을 정도의 격차.
288|
289|그럼에도 저들의 공격을 온전히 피할 수 없으리라는 직감이 들었다.
290|
291|몸이 움직이지 않는 이 와중에도 문득 뇌리를 스치는 어이없는 생각과 함께.
292|
293|‘레벨 업 이거, 혹시 사지가 잘려나가도 회복시켜주나?’
294|

[P56]
*Splash.*

[P57]
“Do you know something?”

[P58]
Sama Pyo sat in the pool of blood and met his father’s eyes. Watching them tremble, he continued slowly.

[P59]
“There is no son in this world who can kill his father.”

[P60]
“…!”

[P61]
“I’ll tell them everything myself. I’ll tell them about the pathetic son who knew of his father’s betrayal and tried not to see it.”

[P62]
“You…”

[P63]
“I’m not asking to be forgiven. I’m going to bear the consequences.”

[P64]
There was such peace in his answer, such acceptance, that Sima Gong could say nothing.

[P65]
He could only struggle to hold back a feeling he’d long forgotten—a feeling he had remembered only here, today.

[P66]
His vision slowly darkened. His breathing grew short.

[P67]
“You asked me why I did it. Why I, who spent my whole life chasing survival and gain, made such a foolish choice…”

[P68]
To save the heir who would inherit everything he had?

[P69]
No. That wasn’t it.

[P70]
At least in that moment, Sima Gong knew there had been another reason.

[P71]
He was simply too late to confess it.

[P72]
“I… This father of yours…”

[P73]
Facing the son who had returned to be with him at the end, Sima Gong used all the strength he had left to force out the words.

[P74]
He didn’t even realize he had drawn his final breath.

[P75]
*Slump.*

[P76]
His head fell to one side.

[P77]
To his father, who had died so wretchedly, as if burdened by the deeds of his life, the son whispered, “I heard you. Clearly.”

[P78]
Sama Pyo’s shoulders began to shake. The pool of blood soaking father and son trembled with them.

[P79]
* * *

[P80]
Highly trained hunting dogs always obey their master’s commands.

[P81]
They fix their eyes on the prey he points out, bare their teeth and growl. The moment he slips their leashes, they race forward and tear into it with all their strength.

[P82]
Until their prey stops breathing.

[P83]
Or until their master orders them to stop and return.

[P84]
Just like now.

[P85]
*Shwaa!*

[P86]
A piercing whistle came from my side, accompanied by a flash of light.

[P87]
But speed was always relative.

[P88]
The Sword Energy surged along a white blade and fell toward the top of my head with all the speed expected of a Peak master. To me, though, it wasn’t fast.

[P89]
*Shhk!*

[P90]
Space split in an instant.

[P91]
A fraction of a beat later came the slicing sound. Everything in the silver-white spearhead’s path had been cut apart.

[P92]
The Sword Energy, snuffed out like a candle in the wind.

[P93]
The blade that had carried that mighty energy.

[P94]
And finally, the body of the man who had made the futile attack.

[P95]
*Fwoosh!*

[P96]
A tremendous fountain of blood burst from his cleanly severed body. I didn’t blink at the sight.

[P97]
Neither did the other hunting dogs charging me from every direction.

[P98]
*Thud, crunch! Whump!*

[P99]
I drove my spearhead into the chest of the first one coming straight at me. With my other hand, I crushed the face of an enemy lunging from my blind spot. Then I yanked the embedded spearhead free and swung it.

[P100]
“Ghk—kgh.”

[P101]
*Thump.*

[P102]
Three Peak masters fell with dying cries in place of last words.

[P103]
No—not three masters.

[P104]
Three corpses.

[P105]
But the frenzy of battle sweeping across the blood-soaked snowfield showed no sign of easing.

[P106]
*Shh-shh-shh-shhk!*

[P107]
The Dark Heaven cultists rushed in to fill the gaps without giving me a moment’s pause.

[P108]
At the sight of their blank faces and eyes devoid of feeling, I felt an exhaustion so deep it weighed down my whole body.

[P109]
*How many is that now?*

[P110]
I had no idea.

[P111]
I had neither the time nor the reason to count every enemy I’d killed.

[P112]
I could only fight. Keep knocking them down.

[P113]
Those soulless wooden puppets.

[P114]
Those hunting dogs, those moths blindly carrying out their final order even though the master who held their leashes was gone.

[P115]
Of course, I knew what this was.

[P116]
A one-sided massacre. Slaughter.

[P117]
But I had to do it.

[P118]
It was the only way to end this bloody battle and save as many of our people as I could.

[P119]
So I clung with all my strength to the thread of consciousness that felt ready to snap at any moment.

[P120]
*Come on.*

[P121]
I called to them in my head and charged.

[P122]
Or tried to.

[P123]
That was when my vision faded.

[P124]
“…!”

[P125]
An alarm blared in my head.

[P126]
My mind had reached its limit long ago. Now it was sending me a warning it could no longer hold back.

[P127]
But by the time I gritted my teeth and forced my eyes wide, it was already too late.

[P128]
*Shwaa!*

[P129]
My view had tilted. A dozen blades were raining down on my body, which had staggered without my even realizing it.

[P130]
They looked faint. Slow.

[P131]
My eyesight was still sharp enough to follow them. The problem was my brain: the part that needed to tell my body to move had frozen like stone.

[P132]
*Damn it.*

[P133]
I cursed inwardly as the world slowed around me.

[P134]
These men were no Blood-Sword Demon Lord or Grand Mage. They couldn’t even compare to the Black Ghosts.

[P135]
They fell far short.

[P136]
Under normal circumstances, I would’ve scoffed at the difference between us.

[P137]
Even so, I knew I couldn’t dodge every blade.

[P138]
And while my body refused to move, one ridiculous thought crossed my mind.

[P139]
*If I level up, would it heal me even if my limbs got cut off?*

[P140]
Fortunately, I didn’t have to worry about that unpleasant first experience—the sort only someone like Cheongpung might enjoy.

[P141]
The next moment, an enormous rush of air sounded from somewhere and swept my worries away.

[P142]
*Whoooosh!*

[P143]
It happened in the blink of an eye.

[P144]
A huge shadow rose over the shoulders of the enemies charging toward me. With it came a two-section staff, big and beautiful just as its name suggested, cleaving through the air like lightning.

[P145]
*Craaaack!*

[P146]
If anyone ever asked whether I’d seen five heads knocked flying with a single swing of a bat, I could nod without hesitation.

[P147]
I could even name the top prospect who’d tear through the modern Major Leagues, now a playground for Awakened Ones.

[P148]
Of course, that lunatic hulk would introduce himself before anyone else got the chance.

[P149]
Just like now.

[P150]
“Taishan! Came! Saw! Hit!”

[P151]
“Well done! Now, Body Slam!”

[P152]
Starting with Namho, perched on the shoulder of Taishan—who had just delivered a line to make Julius Caesar weep—familiar faces burst onto the scene like streaks of light.

[P153]
“Young Master! No, Benefactor! No, Pavilion Master!”

[P154]
*Shhk!*

[P155]
Ju Hwaran split an enemy’s skull while changing how she addressed me three times in a breath. Even a Transformer would’ve struggled to keep up.

[P156]
“Fools! You dare try to harm the Captain? Your courage is admirable, but first you’ll have to get past me—the Captain’s right arm and heart! I, Hyuk Mu—whoa, shit!”

[P157]
*Clang!*

[P158]
Hyuk Mujin had charged in with a grand entrance, only to scramble backward when his opponent’s counterattack proved stronger than he’d expected.

[P159]
“Uh, does that guy know how to fight with his mouth shut?”

[P160]
“You should try shutting yours first.”

[P161]
*Stab, stab!*

[P162]
Song Ilseom and… wait, who was that black, shaggy old guy? Together, they saved Hyuk Mujin and cut down the remaining enemies in a flash.

[P163]
“The Seven Masters of the Black Horse?”

[P164]
The name slipped out before I knew it. The middle-aged man, a former mounted bandit, twisted his already fearsome face.

[P165]
“Not Black Horse—White Horse! I’m Ma Junggeol, eldest of the Seven Masters of Baekma Bang! Who do you think went through all this shit for you? And you forgot me…!”

[P166]
“Lower your voice. While I’m asking nicely.”

[P167]
Ma Junggeol clamped his mouth shut at Ju Hwaran’s chilling warning. A laugh escaped me.

[P168]
It was just good to see them.

[P169]
To know we hadn’t lost anyone.

[P170]
And…

[P171]
To see the last person, the one I’d thought I might never see again.

[P172]
“You made it?”

[P173]
Sama Pyo, who I hadn’t even seen arrive, shrugged.

[P174]
“Am I late?”

[P175]
No.

[P176]
Not at all.

# Mastering Adjudicator Brief

You are a **veto**, not a second novelist and not a gloss writer.

This call is isolated, non-interactive, and tool-free. The packet already contains the Korean source, both complete English versions, glossary matches, rules, and every numbered hunk. Do not call tools, search the repository, or read files. Do not announce a plan.

The first editor (SOL) has already rewritten the accepted English (BASELINE) for fluency. Default is `SOL`. Take `BASE` only when SOL is actually unfaithful. Write `REPAIR` only when **both** BASE and SOL are unfaithful.

## Default

Choose `SOL` unless a veto below fires.

Keep SOL when it is slangier, punchier, more spoken, or more idiomatic and the Korean sense holds (`기만질` → “con me”, `톡톡히` → “full Peak Master treatment”, `득실거리다` → “crawling with”, `인간 백정` → “butcher of men”, `한 몸` → “are one”, `시원하다` in a bath → “That’s the stuff”, `어렵게 찾아오고 쉽게 깨지는 법` → “hard-won and easily broken”). **Literal closeness to Korean wording is not fidelity.** Preserve the source’s meaning and effect in natural English.

## Veto — choose `BASE`

Use `BASE` only for a real miss:

* wrong denotation, quantity, hedge, category, subject/object, or physical action
* a different English idiom than the Korean joke (`까발리다` ≠ “gives someone away”; `넉살` ≠ “banter”)

# Translation Rules

## Fidelity

- Translate the Korean source—not the wiki, manhwa, fan translations, or expected plot.
- Semantic fidelity outranks elegance. Never improve rhythm, humor, or localization by changing a physical action, negation, relationship, hierarchy, mechanism, quantity, or causal detail.
- Preserve every fact, causal link, joke, emotional beat, repetition, and intentional omission. Add nothing.
- Preserve small action verbs and pragmatic cues exactly: nodding versus shaking one's head, pretending nothing happened, and mild or approachable impressions are characterization, not expendable texture.
- Preserve viewpoint and tense. Resolve omitted subjects only when context supports it; retain genuine ambiguity.
- Match each speaker's hierarchy, intimacy, humor, and profanity naturally. Do not mechanically retain every honorific or classical self-reference.
- Do not censor or soften content.

## Terminology

- `compendium.md` and `docs/NAMES.md` are binding for established names, titles, ranks, techniques, organizations, system terms, items, and locations. Profile headings and aliases join that ledger.
- Search only exact Korean terms already present in the current chapter; the compendium contains future-sensitive entries.
- Never re-romanize established names or invent grand names for uncertain terms. First use of an unlisted name or title almost always needs a footnote or a mapped ledger term.
- Use `qi` for Murim energy and `mana` for the modern Hunter system when the source distinguishes them. Preserve an established chapter-specific rendering such as `internal energy` when the exact glossary and surrounding Korean distinguish accumulated `공력` from resulting `기운`.
- In System panels, render `등급` as `**Grade:**` for quest, item, skill, and martial-art classifications. Reserve `rank` for Hunter classifications or ordinary prose; never replace a System `Grade` field with `Rank`.

## English and Markdown

- Use contemporary US English and natural action-comedy prose; avoid Korean syntax calques and generic cultivation MTL phrasing.
- File: `translations/NNNN.md`; heading: `# Chapter N`.
- Speech: curly double quotes. Direct thoughts: italics without quotes.
- Use em dashes without spaces, the ellipsis character `…`, and `* * *` for source scene breaks.
- Format each actual game System-message panel as one Markdown blockquote window headed `> **System**`. Keep all consecutive notices, fields, and lines inside that same blockquote; separate windows when prose intervenes. Do not enclose System notices or UI terms in square brackets; the `System` heading and framed blockquote identify the panel. Do not label manuals, ordinary quotations, warnings printed in a manual, or other non-System material as `System`; use a normal blockquote or a specific heading instead. Do not wrap each complete notice in outer `**`; retain bold only for meaningful labels or emphasis inside the panel.
- Keep the final file English-only reading copy: no audit notes, Korean text, summaries, or model metadata.

### Tone and Style

- Write like a polished commercial webnovel: brisk, vivid, accessible, and easy to read aloud.
- Preserve the series’ contrast between danger and comedy. Let absurdity, bad timing, blunt reactions, and grim situations create dark humor without adding jokes absent from the Korean.
- Jin Taekyung’s narration is conversational, observant, self-mocking, and occasionally profane. It may be irreverent even when the situation is serious.
- Keep deadpan punchlines short and well-timed. Do not explain a joke after delivering it.
- Preserve the source's level of explicitness. A euphemism may remain euphemistic even when its meaning is sexual or crude; do not replace it with more graphic English merely for impact.
- Make dialogue spontaneous and character-specific. Preserve hierarchy and intimacy through word choice, address, rhythm, and restraint—not archaic wuxia English.
- Use strong profanity when the Korean is strong, but neither intensify nor sanitize it. Do not make ordinary lines uniformly vulgar. Profanity should reveal mood or relationship.
- Keep action and injury vivid but clear rather than purple. Do not make violence funny unless the source’s framing does.
- Avoid stiff literalism, translator-added melodrama, dated internet slang, and quippy superhero-style banter.
- On the second pass, correct awkward English collocations and word choices without changing meaning or voice. Prefer ordinary, spoken English over stiff Latinate or ceremonial wording when the scene is brisk or comic: “goose bumps” rather than “gooseflesh,” and “laid into them” rather than “launched into a solemn denunciation.” Read the prose aloud and replace any phrase that sounds like a formal essay, legal document, or literal dictionary gloss unless the source deliberately calls for that register.

Use `[^1]` Markdown footnotes when a brief, factual, spoiler-free explanation materially helps an English reader understand:

- a Korean institution, living arrangement, food, holiday, myth, historical reference, or local custom;
- a Korean word, phrase, idiom, wordplay, or culturally specific image that cannot be conveyed fully by the best natural English analogy;
- a deliberately literal rendering whose cultural or linguistic force would otherwise be lost.

Footnotes must be rare, useful, and non-spoiling; do not footnote ordinary vocabulary, fully preserved jokes, or uncertainty. Record consequential uncertainty in `docs/STATE.md`.

## Spoilers and Scope

- Future knowledge may prevent contradiction but may not add early names, pronouns, certainty, motives, or foreshadowing.

Sama Pyo sat in the pool of blood and met his father’s eyes. Watching them tremble, he continued slowly.

[P59]
“There is no son in this world who can kill his father.”

[P60]
“…!”

[P61]
“I’ll tell them everything myself. I’ll tell them about the pathetic son who knew of his father’s betrayal and tried not to see it.”

[P62]
“You…”

[P63]
“I’m not asking to be forgiven. I’m going to bear the consequences.”

[P64]
There was such peace in his answer, such acceptance, that Sima Gong could say nothing.

[P65]
He could only struggle to hold back a feeling he’d long forgotten—a feeling he had remembered only here, today.

[P66]
His vision slowly darkened. His breathing grew short.

[P67]
“You asked me why I did it. Why I, who spent my whole life chasing survival and gain, made such a foolish choice…”

[P68]
To save the heir who would inherit everything he had?

[P69]
No. That wasn’t it.

[P70]
At least in that moment, Sima Gong knew there had been another reason.

[P71]
He was simply too late to confess it.

[P72]
“I… This father of yours…”

[P73]
Facing the son who had returned to be with him at the end, Sima Gong used all the strength he had left to force out the words.

[P74]
He didn’t even realize he had drawn his final breath.

[P75]
*Slump.*

[P76]
His head fell to one side.

[P77]
To his father, who had died so wretchedly, as if burdened by the deeds of his life, the son whispered, “I heard you. Clearly.”

[P78]
Sama Pyo’s shoulders began to shake. The pool of blood soaking father and son trembled with them.

[P79]
* * *

[P80]
Highly trained hunting dogs always obey their master’s commands.

[P81]
They fix their eyes on the prey he points out, bare their teeth and growl. The moment he slips their leashes, they race forward and tear into it with all their strength.

[P82]
Until their prey stops breathing.

[P83]
Or until their master orders them to stop and return.

[P84]
Just like now.

[P85]
*Shwaa!*

[P86]
A piercing whistle came from my side, accompanied by a flash of light.

[P87]
But speed was always relative.

[P88]
The Sword Energy surged along a white blade and fell toward the top of my head with all the speed expected of a Peak master. To me, though, it wasn’t fast.

[P89]
*Shhk!*

[P90]
Space split in an instant.

[P91]
A fraction of a beat later came the slicing sound. Everything in the silver-white spearhead’s path had been cut apart.

[P92]
The Sword Energy, snuffed out like a candle in the wind.

[P93]
The blade that had carried that mighty energy.

[P94]
And finally, the body of the man who had made the futile attack.

[P95]
*Fwoosh!*

[P96]
A tremendous fountain of blood burst from his cleanly severed body. I didn’t blink at the sight.

[P97]
Neither did the other hunting dogs charging me from every direction.

[P98]
*Thud, crunch! Whump!*

[P99]
I drove my spearhead into the chest of the first one coming straight at me. With my other hand, I crushed the face of an enemy lunging from my blind spot. Then I yanked the embedded spearhead free and swung it.

[P100]
“Ghk—kgh.”

[P101]
*Thump.*

[P102]
Three Peak masters fell with dying cries in place of last words.

[P103]
No—not three masters.

[P104]
Three corpses.

[P105]
But the frenzy of battle sweeping across the blood-soaked snowfield showed no sign of easing.

[P106]
*Shh-shh-shh-shhk!*

[P107]
The Dark Heaven cultists rushed in to fill the gaps without giving me a moment’s pause.

[P108]
At the sight of their blank faces and eyes devoid of feeling, I felt an exhaustion so deep it weighed down my whole body.

[P109]
*How many is that now?*

[P110]
I had no idea.

[P111]
I had neither the time nor the reason to count every enemy I’d killed.

[P112]
I could only fight. Keep knocking them down.

[P113]
Those soulless wooden puppets.

[P114]
Those hunting dogs, those moths blindly carrying out their final order even though the master who held their leashes was gone.

[P115]
Of course, I knew what this was.

[P116]
A one-sided massacre. Slaughter.

[P117]
But I had to do it.

[P118]
It was the only way to end this bloody battle and save as many of our people as I could.

[P119]
So I clung with all my strength to the thread of consciousness that felt ready to snap at any moment.

[P120]
*Come on.*

[P121]
I called to them in my head and charged.

[P122]
Or tried to.

[P123]
That was when my vision faded.

[P124]
“…!”

[P125]
An alarm blared in my head.

[P126]
My mind had reached its limit long ago. Now it was sending me a warning it could no longer hold back.

[P127]
But by the time I gritted my teeth and forced my eyes wide, it was already too late.

[P128]
*Shwaa!*

[P129]
My view had tilted. A dozen blades were raining down on my body, which had staggered without my even realizing it.

[P130]
They looked faint. Slow.

[P131]
My eyesight was still sharp enough to follow them. The problem was my brain: the part that needed to tell my body to move had frozen like stone.

[P132]
*Damn it.*

[P133]
I cursed inwardly as the world slowed around me.

[P134]
These men were no Blood-Sword Demon Lord or Grand Mage. They couldn’t even compare to the Black Ghosts.

[P135]
They fell far short.

[P136]
Under normal circumstances, I would’ve scoffed at the difference between us.

[P137]
Even so, I knew I couldn’t dodge every blade.

[P138]
And while my body refused to move, one ridiculous thought crossed my mind.

[P139]
*If I level up, would it heal me even if my limbs got cut off?*

[P140]
Fortunately, I didn’t have to worry about that unpleasant first experience—the sort only someone like Cheongpung might enjoy.

[P141]
The next moment, an enormous rush of air sounded from somewhere and swept my worries away.

[P142]
*Whoooosh!*

[P143]
It happened in the blink of an eye.

[P144]
A huge shadow rose over the shoulders of the enemies charging toward me. With it came a two-section staff, big and beautiful just as its name suggested, cleaving through the air like lightning.

[P145]
*Craaaack!*

[P146]
If anyone ever asked whether I’d seen five heads knocked flying with a single swing of a bat, I could nod without hesitation.

[P147]
I could even name the top prospect who’d tear through the modern Major Leagues, now a playground for Awakened Ones.

[P148]
Of course, that lunatic hulk would introduce himself before anyone else got the chance.

[P149]
Just like now.

[P150]
“Taishan! Came! Saw! Hit!”

[P151]
“Well done! Now, Body Slam!”

[P152]
Starting with Namho, perched on the shoulder of Taishan—who had just delivered a line to make Julius Caesar weep—familiar faces burst onto the scene like streaks of light.

[P153]
“Young Master! No, Benefactor! No, Pavilion Master!”

[P154]
*Shhk!*

[P155]
Ju Hwaran split an enemy’s skull while changing how she addressed me three times in a breath. Even a Transformer would’ve struggled to keep up.

[P156]
“Fools! You dare try to harm the Captain? Your courage is admirable, but first you’ll have to get past me—the Captain’s right arm and heart! I, Hyuk Mu—whoa, shit!”

[P157]
*Clang!*

[P158]
Hyuk Mujin had charged in with a grand entrance, only to scramble backward when his opponent’s counterattack proved stronger than he’d expected.

[P159]
“Uh, does that guy know how to fight with his mouth shut?”

[P160]
“You should try shutting yours first.”

[P161]
*Stab, stab!*

[P162]
Song Ilseom and… wait, who was that black, shaggy old guy? Together, they saved Hyuk Mujin and cut down the remaining enemies in a flash.

[P163]
“The Seven Masters of the Black Horse?”

[P164]
The name slipped out before I knew it. The middle-aged man, a former mounted bandit, twisted his already fearsome face.

[P165]
“Not Black Horse—White Horse! I’m Ma Junggeol, eldest of the Seven Masters of Baekma Bang! Who do you think went through all this shit for you? And you forgot me…!”

[P166]
“Lower your voice. While I’m asking nicely.”

[P167]
Ma Junggeol clamped his mouth shut at Ju Hwaran’s chilling warning. A laugh escaped me.

[P168]
It was just good to see them.

[P169]
To know we hadn’t lost anyone.

[P170]
And…

[P171]
To see the last person, the one I’d thought I might never see again.

[P172]
“You made it?”

[P173]
Sama Pyo, who I hadn’t even seen arrive, shrugged.

[P174]
“Am I late?”

[P175]
No.

[P176]
Not at all.

# Mastering Adjudicator Brief

You are a **veto**, not a second novelist and not a gloss writer.

This call is isolated, non-interactive, and tool-free. The packet already contains the Korean source, both complete English versions, glossary matches, rules, and every numbered hunk. Do not call tools, search the repository, or read files. Do not announce a plan.

The first editor (SOL) has already rewritten the accepted English (BASELINE) for fluency. Default is `SOL`. Take `BASE` only when SOL is actually unfaithful. Write `REPAIR` only when **both** BASE and SOL are unfaithful.

## Default

Choose `SOL` unless a veto below fires.

Keep SOL when it is slangier, punchier, more spoken, or more idiomatic and the Korean sense holds (`기만질` → “con me”, `톡톡히` → “full Peak Master treatment”, `득실거리다` → “crawling with”, `인간 백정` → “butcher of men”, `한 몸` → “are one”, `시원하다` in a bath → “That’s the stuff”, `어렵게 찾아오고 쉽게 깨지는 법` → “hard-won and easily broken”). **Literal closeness to Korean wording is not fidelity.** Preserve the source’s meaning and effect in natural English.

## Veto — choose `BASE`

Use `BASE` only for a real miss:

* wrong denotation, quantity, hedge, category, subject/object, or physical action
* a different English idiom than the Korean joke (`까발리다` ≠ “gives someone away”; `넉살` ≠ “banter”)

# Translation Rules

## Fidelity

- Translate the Korean source—not the wiki, manhwa, fan translations, or expected plot.
- Semantic fidelity outranks elegance. Never improve rhythm, humor, or localization by changing a physical action, negation, relationship, hierarchy, mechanism, quantity, or causal detail.
- Preserve every fact, causal link, joke, emotional beat, repetition, and intentional omission. Add nothing.
- Preserve small action verbs and pragmatic cues exactly: nodding versus shaking one's head, pretending nothing happened, and mild or approachable impressions are characterization, not expendable texture.
- Preserve viewpoint and tense. Resolve omitted subjects only when context supports it; retain genuine ambiguity.
- Match each speaker's hierarchy, intimacy, humor, and profanity naturally. Do not mechanically retain every honorific or classical self-reference.
- Do not censor or soften content.

## Terminology

- `compendium.md` and `docs/NAMES.md` are binding for established names, titles, ranks, techniques, organizations, system terms, items, and locations. Profile headings and aliases join that ledger.
- Search only exact Korean terms already present in the current chapter; the compendium contains future-sensitive entries.
- Never re-romanize established names or invent grand names for uncertain terms. First use of an unlisted name or title almost always needs a footnote or a mapped ledger term.
- Use `qi` for Murim energy and `mana` for the modern Hunter system when the source distinguishes them. Preserve an established chapter-specific rendering such as `internal energy` when the exact glossary and surrounding Korean distinguish accumulated `공력` from resulting `기운`.
- In System panels, render `등급` as `**Grade:**` for quest, item, skill, and martial-art classifications. Reserve `rank` for Hunter classifications or ordinary prose; never replace a System `Grade` field with `Rank`.

## English and Markdown

- Use contemporary US English and natural action-comedy prose; avoid Korean syntax calques and generic cultivation MTL phrasing.
- File: `translations/NNNN.md`; heading: `# Chapter N`.
- Speech: curly double quotes. Direct thoughts: italics without quotes.
- Use em dashes without spaces, the ellipsis character `…`, and `* * *` for source scene breaks.
- Format each actual game System-message panel as one Markdown blockquote window headed `> **System**`. Keep all consecutive notices, fields, and lines inside that same blockquote; separate windows when prose intervenes. Do not enclose System notices or UI terms in square brackets; the `System` heading and framed blockquote identify the panel. Do not label manuals, ordinary quotations, warnings printed in a manual, or other non-System material as `System`; use a normal blockquote or a specific heading instead. Do not wrap each complete notice in outer `**`; retain bold only for meaningful labels or emphasis inside the panel.
- Keep the final file English-only reading copy: no audit notes, Korean text, summaries, or model metadata.

### Tone and Style

- Write like a polished commercial webnovel: brisk, vivid, accessible, and easy to read aloud.
- Preserve the series’ contrast between danger and comedy. Let absurdity, bad timing, blunt reactions, and grim situations create dark humor without adding jokes absent from the Korean.
- Jin Taekyung’s narration is conversational, observant, self-mocking, and occasionally profane. It may be irreverent even when the situation is serious.
- Keep deadpan punchlines short and well-timed. Do not explain a joke after delivering it.
- Preserve the source's level of explicitness. A euphemism may remain euphemistic even when its meaning is sexual or crude; do not replace it with more graphic English merely for impact.
- Make dialogue spontaneous and character-specific. Preserve hierarchy and intimacy through word choice, address, rhythm, and restraint—not archaic wuxia English.
- Use strong profanity when the Korean is strong, but neither intensify nor sanitize it. Do not make ordinary lines uniformly vulgar. Profanity should reveal mood or relationship.
- Keep action and injury vivid but clear rather than purple. Do not make violence funny unless the source’s framing does.
- Avoid stiff literalism, translator-added melodrama, dated internet slang, and quippy superhero-style banter.
- On the second pass, correct awkward English collocations and word choices without changing meaning or voice. Prefer ordinary, spoken English over stiff Latinate or ceremonial wording when the scene is brisk or comic: “goose bumps” rather than “gooseflesh,” and “laid into them” rather than “launched into a solemn denunciation.” Read the prose aloud and replace any phrase that sounds like a formal essay, legal document, or literal dictionary gloss unless the source deliberately calls for that register.

Use `[^1]` Markdown footnotes when a brief, factual, spoiler-free explanation materially helps an English reader understand:

- a Korean institution, living arrangement, food, holiday, myth, historical reference, or local custom;
- a Korean word, phrase, idiom, wordplay, or culturally specific image that cannot be conveyed fully by the best natural English analogy;

Footnotes must be rare, useful, and non-spoiling; do not footnote ordinary vocabulary, fully preserved jokes, or uncertainty. Record consequential uncertainty in `docs/STATE.md`.

- Future knowledge may prevent contradiction but may not add early names, pronouns, certainty, motives, or foreshadowing.

# Translation Rules

## Fidelity

- Translate the Korean source—not the wiki, manhwa, fan translations, or expected plot.
- Semantic fidelity outranks elegance. Never improve rhythm, humor, or localization by changing a physical action, negation, relationship, hierarchy, mechanism, quantity, or causal detail.
- Preserve every fact, causal link, joke, emotional beat, repetition, and intentional omission. Add nothing.
- Preserve small action verbs and pragmatic cues exactly: nodding versus shaking one's head, pretending nothing happened, and mild or approachable impressions are characterization, not expendable texture.
- Preserve viewpoint and tense. Resolve omitted subjects only when context supports it; retain genuine ambiguity.
- Match each speaker's hierarchy, intimacy, humor, and profanity naturally. Do not mechanically retain every honorific or classical self-reference.
- Do not censor or soften content.

## Terminology

- `compendium.md` and `docs/NAMES.md` are binding for established names, titles, ranks, techniques, organizations, system terms, items, and locations. Profile headings and aliases join that ledger.
- Search only exact Korean terms already present in the current chapter; the compendium contains future-sensitive entries.
- Never re-romanize established names or invent grand names for uncertain terms. First use of an unlisted name or title almost always needs a footnote or a mapped ledger term.
- Use `qi` for Murim energy and `mana` for the modern Hunter system when the source distinguishes them. Preserve an established chapter-specific rendering such as `internal energy` when the exact glossary and surrounding Korean distinguish accumulated `공력` from resulting `기운`.
- In System panels, render `등급` as `**Grade:**` for quest, item, skill, and martial-art classifications. Reserve `rank` for Hunter classifications or ordinary prose; never replace a System `Grade` field with `Rank`.

## English and Markdown

- Use contemporary US English and natural action-comedy prose; avoid Korean syntax calques and generic cultivation MTL phrasing.
- File: `translations/NNNN.md`; heading: `# Chapter N`.
- Speech: curly double quotes. Direct thoughts: italics without quotes.
- Use em dashes without spaces, the ellipsis character `…`, and `* * *` for source scene breaks.
- Format each actual game System-message panel as one Markdown blockquote window headed `> **System**`. Keep all consecutive notices, fields, and lines inside that same blockquote; separate windows when prose intervenes. Do not enclose System notices or UI terms in square brackets; the `System` heading and framed blockquote identify the panel. Do not label manuals, ordinary quotations, warnings printed in a manual, or other non-System material as `System`; use a normal blockquote or a specific heading instead. Do not wrap each complete notice in outer `**`; retain bold only for meaningful labels or emphasis inside the panel.
- Keep the final file English-only reading copy: no audit notes, Korean text, summaries, or model metadata.

### Tone and Style

- Write like a polished commercial webnovel: brisk, vivid, accessible, and easy to read aloud.
- Preserve the series’ contrast between danger and comedy. Let absurdity, bad timing, blunt reactions, and grim situations create dark humor without adding jokes absent from the Korean.
- Jin Taekyung’s narration is conversational, observant, self-mocking, and occasionally profane. It may be irreverent even when the situation is serious.
- Keep deadpan punchlines short and well-timed. Do not explain a joke after delivering it.
- Preserve the source's level of explicitness. A euphemism may remain euphemistic even when its meaning is sexual or crude; do not replace it with more graphic English merely for impact.
- Make dialogue spontaneous and character-specific. Preserve hierarchy and intimacy through word choice, address, rhythm, and restraint—not archaic wuxia English.
- Use strong profanity when the Korean is strong, but neither intensify nor sanitize it. Do not make ordinary lines uniformly vulgar. Profanity should reveal mood or relationship.
- Keep action and injury vivid but clear rather than purple. Do not make violence funny unless the source’s framing does.
- Avoid stiff literalism, translator-added melodrama, dated internet slang, and quippy superhero-style banter.
- On the second pass, correct awkward English collocations and word choices without changing meaning or voice. Prefer ordinary, spoken English over stiff Latinate or ceremonial wording when the scene is brisk or comic: “goose bumps” rather than “gooseflesh,” and “laid into them” rather than “launched into a solemn denunciation.” Read the prose aloud and replace any phrase that sounds like a formal essay, legal document, or literal dictionary gloss unless the source deliberately calls for that register.

## Footnotes

Use `[^1]` Markdown footnotes when a brief, factual, spoiler-free explanation materially helps an English reader understand:

- a Korean institution, living arrangement, food, holiday, myth, historical reference, or local custom;
- a Korean word, phrase, idiom, wordplay, or culturally specific image that cannot be conveyed fully by the best natural English analogy;
- a deliberately literal rendering whose cultural or linguistic force would otherwise be lost.

For example, render `고시원` as “goshiwon” when the setting or connotations matter, with a concise footnote explaining that it is a very small, inexpensive room-for-rent housing arrangement. Prefer the best natural English analogy in the prose. Use a literal translation plus a concise footnote when the Korean wording itself matters. Define a term at its first meaningful occurrence and do not repeat the note unnecessarily. Footnotes must be rare, useful, and non-spoiling; do not footnote ordinary vocabulary, fully preserved jokes, or uncertainty. Record consequential uncertainty in `docs/STATE.md`.

## Spoilers and Scope

- Safe profiles contain only facts revealed through the latest completed chapter.
- Never read `characters/spoilers/` during drafting. Reviewers may consult one relevant sealed profile only for a specific unresolved continuity issue after the draft is complete.
- Future knowledge may prevent contradiction but may not add early names, pronouns, certainty, motives, or foreshadowing.
- Translate exactly one requested chapter unless the user explicitly requests a batch. Never modify Korean source files under `source/`.
